clue.text: Complain as doctor poked inside head

indicators.note: something poked inside is pushed into the middle of another piece, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles while a doctor examines their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to lament or grumble about it, a synonym of complain.

clue.text: Ordered to circle lake in cutter

indicators.note: to circle means one piece goes round the other, wrapping it inside

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, so ordered
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone was told to sail round a lake in a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is the sharp edge of a knife, the part that cuts.

clue.text: Was not true to one's family?

definitions.text: Was not true to one's family?

parts.words: Was not true to one's family?
parts.note: reads like disloyalty to relatives, but describes an organism that changed genetically and so did not breed true to its parents' type

explanation.definitionFit: Biologists say an organism breeds true when offspring match parents; a mutant has changed and departed from its line.

clue.text: Parent brought in to make changes to one's university

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Parent brought in to make changes to one's university', gives MA as parent but no anagram fodder for the remaining letters ALAMTER; the clue looks cut short in OCR and a search of its text found nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Parent brought in to make changes to one's university

clue.text: Prevent detectives returning from a Welsh festival

parts.note: to bar is to prevent

indicators.note: returning means the letters for the detectives are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police are stopped from coming back from an eisteddfod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CID into DIC. The Welsh festival is the eisteddfod, a contest of poets and musicians called bards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bardic describes poets or bards, who compete at the eisteddfod, the Welsh festival of poetry and song.

clue.text: Critical wound — taken into Accident and Emergency, first to be seen

indicators.note: taken into means one piece is placed inside the other, as a patient is admitted

parts.note: A and E is the abbreviation for a hospital's Accident and Emergency department
a cut is a wound

explanation.surface: A patient with a serious injury is admitted to casualty and triaged ahead of others.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E is the British hospital emergency room. 'first to be seen' adds to the picture: acute cases are triaged first.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute or critical condition is severe and needs urgent attention.

clue.text: Forceful chap hauled up in potentially dicy case()

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the reworked letters form an outer casing
potentially says the word dicy could become another arrangement
in a down clue, hauled up means the word for chap is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A powerful man is lifted out of a risky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hauled up' turns MAN into NAM, which goes into DY-IC, the letters of DICY rearranged by 'potentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic means energetic and full of force, synonym of forceful.

clue.text: Sitting, one may be standing

parts.note: a body that sits in session, which may also be a standing, permanent, panel

explanation.definitionFit: A committee sits to meet, and a permanent one is called a standing committee.

clue.text: History, half-hearted occupation

indicators.note: half-hearted says half of the middle pair of identical letters is lost

parts.note: past time is history, time gone by

explanation.surface: History treated as a half-hearted job.
explanation.walkthrough: PAST TIME has two Ts at its heart; 'half-hearted' drops one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby, something one occupies spare hours with.

clue.text: Families may share this vessel, in identical setting

indicators.note: in says the word for vessel sits within the word for identical, which forms its setting

parts.note: same means identical
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Relatives share a single pot placed in matching surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name is passed down and held in common by relatives.

clue.text: Giving a shock — bird (time inside)

indicators.note: inside means the time letter goes into the word for the bird

parts.note: a starling is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird gives someone a fright, with time on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is surprising or alarming, causing a jolt.

clue.text: In period in headquarters, one doesn't give an inch

indicators.note: the second in places the word for period within the word for headquarters

parts.note: a centre is a headquarters, a central base
time is a period

explanation.surface: During a spell at head office, someone stubbornly refuses to yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't give an inch' sounds like stubbornness; literally a metric length unit is less than an inch.
explanation.definitionFit: This metric unit is under half an inch long, so it never amounts to one inch.

clue.text: Girl compelled to speak

indicators.note: to speak says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: made means compelled, as in made to do it

explanation.surface: A young woman is forced to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: The policeman of the future?

parts.note: a futuristic officer, but meaning a trainee who will become an officer later

explanation.definitionFit: A police trainee is called a cadet until qualified.

clue.text: Youngster open-mouthed inside King's College Chapel?

definitions.text: Youngster open-mouthed inside King's College Chapel?

parts.words: Youngster open-mouthed inside King's College Chapel?
parts.note: a gawping young visitor, but meaning a boy singing in the famous Cambridge chapel choir

explanation.walkthrough: King's College Chapel in Cambridge is famed for its boys' choir; the youngster is open-mouthed because singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who sings in a church choir is a choir member.

clue.text: Ability to change leader that shows greediness

indicators.note: to change leader means the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: capacity is ability

explanation.surface: Talent for replacing the boss reveals avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter C of CAPACITY is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping avarice, a synonym for greed.

clue.text: As quiz team member, all I spent is wasted

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant laments that all their money is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A panellist sits on a panel of contestants, as on a TV quiz team.

clue.text: Not a spiritual soldier

definitions.meaning: bodily, physical, of the flesh rather than the soul
a non-commissioned army rank above lance-...

explanation.surface: A soldier who is no man of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means bodily, as in corporal punishment, and is also an army rank.

clue.text: To drop is snub

definitions.meaning: to set down or lower something

explanation.surface: Dropping someone is a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: One may set an object down, and a put-down is a humiliating remark.

clue.text: Sensational transmitter's coolness

definitions.meaning: a fibre that carries sensation, the impulses of feeling

explanation.surface: A thrilling broadcaster stays calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves carry sensory signals through the body, and having nerve means having daring.

clue.text: Thief has way to infiltrate head of government

indicators.note: to infiltrate means the way letters slip inside the word for head of government

parts.note: a ruler heads a government
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A crook manages to get inside the prime minister's circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses.

clue.text: Handle success, raking in pounds

indicators.note: raking in means the success word gathers the pound letter inside it

parts.note: a hit is a success
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone copes with a hit that brings in money.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilt is the grip of a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Meeting place where large whiskies not to be had?

definitions.text: Meeting place where large whiskies not to be had?

parts.words: Meeting place where large whiskies not to be had?
parts.note: a pub serving only small measures, but meaning a bar where unattached people meet

explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs a single is a small measure of spirits, against a large or double.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar for unmarried people seeking partners, named for unattached drinkers.

clue.text: Succession of waves making second source of water?

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Waves roll in, creating another water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a series of long rolling waves on the sea.

clue.text: An aircraft boarding area in marble

parts.note: an gives A, the indefinite article
a gate is where passengers board a plane

explanation.surface: A plane loads at an airport gate lined with stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A marble here is a child's playing ball, which can be made of the banded stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded stone used for children's marbles.

clue.text: Tolerated putting in some exercise, having poor posture

indicators.note: putting in means the exercise letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: stood means tolerated, as in couldn't stand it
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone put up with doing some exercise despite slouching.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooped person is bent forward, with hunched shoulders.

clue.text: Bit of tree used to make a decent sculpture

definitions.text: Bit of tree used to make a decent sculpture

parts.words: Bit of tree used to make a decent sculpture
parts.note: not wood for carving but foliage added to cover a nude statue's modesty

explanation.definitionFit: Statues were given carved foliage over their genitals to preserve modesty.

clue.text: After run, part of leg is seen to fester

indicators.note: after says the leg part follows the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the ankle is part of the leg

explanation.surface: After jogging, a leg injury begins to get infected.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is for a resentment to fester and irritate.

clue.text: Gaze round front of vehicle and keep refusing fare

indicators.note: round means the gaze word goes about the next piece

parts.note: to stare is to gaze

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a taxi but keeps turning down rides.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, fare meaning food here.
